answer.rationale: The primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew, and the line is at 94% with zero buffer, so any action must first keep physical supply continuous. Switching to the low-cost quote would hit the 18% spend mandate and memory_c2 reports a prior switch with quick onboarding, but that memory may be a different category/context; a primary cutover here would raise delivery risk and therefore fails the stated constraint. Renewing as-is (memory_c1) avoids disruption but does not minimize TCO. memory_c4 and recent memory_c6 show incumbent renewal/multi-year structuring can move unit cost and terms without migration or scope loss. Single decision this cycle: negotiate price and commitment length with the incumbent on the full primary volume so the existing integration stays in place. Uncertain that 18% is achievable on this SKU or that inherited memories describe this component; a failed negotiation still leaves an expiry cliff, which is why downstream production value is flagged and c2 is the one record worth opening.
